Dorking have several really good members—Read completing a triple win by taking the 100 and 220 yds. and the long jump at 18ft. Harrold won the quarter in 53 which was only 3/5ths slower than the senior quarter.
The latter, however, won the 220 with Ted Read in second place. Morris, the Police champion, won the 880 Yards and Alf Orton ran well to credit us with third place.
Our lads had turned up in good strength, and with Read and Dumbrill, we had first two home in both sprint races. Len Marchant ran a grand race to beat the Police champion, D.
The 100 Yards Club Championship was won by Ted Read, who beat Dicky Dumbrill with Jack Frost third, and the holder, Stan Botwright, beaten into fourth place.
Higgins, the Public Schools' quarter champion, beat Ted Read in the 220, and scored a double by also winning the 440, in which Jack Frost finished third.

In the 4 x 100 Yards Relay our four ran second to Achilles, our runners were Teddy Read, Dicky Dumbrill, Jack Frost and Michael Broadbent. Another Relay success was at Guildford, Lulham, Hawkins, Osmint and Read each pulled away from their rivals.

We have the talent, some of it already shown, some of it dormant, but to mention only these few names is to comment on a strength which could do much: Broadbent, Botwright, Burfitt, Blowfield, Nankeville, Marchant, Herbert, Read, Lucas, Stimpson.

Our Stan Vickers, the Championship holder, started at a tremendous pace and at one mile had a lead of about thirty yards over a small group consisting of Eric Hall, Matthews (Sutton Coldfield) and Norman Read(Steyning), the Olympic 50 kms.
